name: Slovak
catalog_quote: The stress rule operates on prosodic words as a whole, so affixes are stress-sensitive.
sweep_summary: Slovak (slov1269) is in the catalog as fixed-strict initial stress with an alternating secondary profile, the deciding text being an StressTyp2 paraphrase of Dogil (1999) rather than a quotation. The sweep produced one bibliography item: Sabol, J. 1981, 'The Prosodic Structure of the Slovak Word', Prague Studies in Mathematical Linguistics 7 (LLSEE 9), pp. 59-80, John Benjamins, doi:10.1075/llsee.9.05sab. It is relevant (word stress of Slovak, by the principal Slovak prosodist) but closed: Unpaywall and Semantic Scholar both report no open copy and no abstract; Benjamins (Cloudflare block) and De Gruyter (empty response) are unreachable from our machine; HathiTrust has no record for either ISBN; archive.org holds only vol. 1 (1966); Open Library shows no ebook; Google Books API quota was exhausted. Records (, blocked landing pages, HathiTrust/Google Books responses) and. Priority for acquisition: medium — an English-language first-hand statement, but the same author's fuller stress article (Sabol 1986, SAS 15:391-412) is already on file and was re-read: it states fixed first-syllable stress (p. 392), prosodic-word domain with stressed monosyllabic prepositions (p. 405), and denies systemic secondary stress (pp. 395-396, citing Petreková 1986), while quoting Kráľ 1984:164's orthoepic 3rd/penult secondary stress. That held statement confirms the catalog's initial primary stress and WORD domain and contradicts its 101/10101 secondary profile; it supersedes the StressTyp2/Dogil paraphrase as the deciding source. all findings come from DOI/API records and pages actually opened.

new_statements.quote: Prízvuk je v spisovnej slovenčine fixný, viazaný na prvú slabiku slova (Zajtra pôjdeme domov). Viazanosť prízvuku v slovenčine vylučuje jeho schopnosť rozlišovať význam (na rozdiel od jazykov s voľným prízvukom, napríklad ruštiny). Fixné miesto prízvuku na 1. slabike slova a tvaru rozhodujúcim spôsobom určuje prozodický charakter spisovnej slovenčiny [...] Experimentálny prieskum intenzity kriviek pri analýze slovenského prízvuku (Petreková, 1986) však ukazuje, že tzv. vedľajší prízvuk v spisovnej slovenčine neexistuje ako systémový jav.
new_statements.translation: Stress in standard Slovak is fixed, bound to the first syllable of the word (Zajtra pôjdeme domov 'Tomorrow we go home'). The boundness of stress in Slovak excludes its ability to distinguish meaning (unlike languages with free stress, e.g. Russian). The fixed place of stress on the 1st syllable of the word and word-form decisively determines the prosodic character of standard Slovak [...] Experimental examination of intensity curves in the analysis of Slovak stress (Petreková 1986), however, shows that so-called secondary stress does not exist in standard Slovak as a systemic phenomenon.
new_statements.citation: Sabol, Ján. 1986. Prízvuk v slovenčine. In J. Mistrík (ed.), Studia Academica Slovaca 15, 391-412. Bratislava: Alfa.
new_statements.locator: p. 392, sect. 1.0 (txt lines 13421-13426); secondary stress p. 395-396, sect. 2.1 (txt lines 13533-13557)
new_statements.reading: First-hand statement by the leading Slovak phonetician: primary stress is fixed on the first syllable of the (prosodic) word, non-contrastive; monosyllabic prepositions normally take the stress (sect. 3.3.1, p. 405), so the domain is the prosodic word, matching the catalog's WORD domain and 'fixed-strict' initial coding. On secondary stress Sabol explicitly rejects any systemic secondary stress (ratio 1 : n-1), while quoting the orthoepic codification (Kráľ 1984:164) that places a weaker secondary stress on the 3rd syllable of 4-syllable words and the 3rd or penultimate of longer words. Neither position yields the catalog's alternating-with-final profile (101, 10101...). This is the same reading the 2026-09-16 audit reached; this sweep adds nothing new because the one target (Sabol 1981) is closed.

audit.recode_to: Primary-initial fixed stays. Secondary profile: drop the alternating '+final' odd-syllable pattern (10 101 1010 10101...). Default recode to initial-only '10 100 1000 10000 100000 1000000 10000000' following Sabol 1986:395-396 and Sabol & Zimmermann 1994 (secondary stress 'neexistuje ako systemovy jav'; ratio 1:n-1), with a caution note carrying the orthoepic alternative from Kral 1984:164 (4-syl 1010; 5+ third-or-penult, e.g. 10100~10010) as a register-dependent variant. Under no Slovak source seen is a trisyllable 101 or a final syllable secondary-stressed, so at minimum n=3,5,7 must change.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work

(2) Deciding source: a 2015 database paraphrase of a 1999 areal-survey chapter (Dogil in van der Hulst), not held. sources.quote: Instrumental (duration, intensity, F0 on CSL 4300; 50 and 28 listeners): stress perceived as 'prizvucnej slabiky (v spisovnej slovencine prva slabika slova) a dalsich neprizvucnych slabik az do konca slova'; intensity and F0 carry stress, duration nil. Models words as one stressed initial syllable followed by unstressed syllables; no secondary-stress positions are posited or measured.
